thread:
Olivia H.: heads-up, mirror-playback run popped a weird delta vs prod for kernel selection + kv warmup. p95 latency up ~18% on a small cohort, need eyes
Sam K.: ugh. is this the run from last night? link?
Olivia H.: yep, 1719198000 run. gist with configs: https://rwd.gists/ab12cd. TL;DR: mirror-mode enabled, sample_cohort=small_users, seed not set in harness (we use timestamp-based seeding)
Lee R.: does the harness set model_variant hints? kernel selector can pick a different GEMM path if seq-len distribution shifts
Olivia H.: config excerpt in gist but copy: ```
--mode mirrorplayback 
--sample-filter "cohort=small_users" 
--anon-level high 
--kernel-hints from_trace=true 
--seed auto_timestamp 
--kv-prewarm true
```
Sam K.: two quick suspects: (1) anon transform changed tokenization lengths -> kernel choice drift, (2) kv prewarm timing different in harness vs prod causing cold misses
Anya P.: PerfBot posted the run metrics: 
PerfBot: run=1719198000, cohort=small_users, throughput=420 tok/s, p50=28ms, p95=142ms, kernel_mix=[fused_gemm:32%, aten_gemm:68%], kv_hit_rate=0.62, checksum_mismatch=0.04
Sam K.: checksum_mismatch 4% is big. Is that checksum on final tokens or intermediate logits?
PerfBot: checksum applies to tokenized output hashes after detokenization (post-filtering).
Lee R.: 0.62 kv hit is low for small_users - production usually shows ~0.78 for that cohort at same hour. Are we sampling the same traffic window?
Olivia H.: harness used a 10% sample across 02:00-03:00 UTC. Prod metrics I'm comparing are for 01:45-02:15 UTC. Slight misalign but shouldn't explain kernel mix swap entirely
Sam K.: can you re-run with: fix seed=42, set anon-level=low (to avoid length shuffles), and force kernel-hints off so the selector uses deterministic fallback? Command: ```
./harness --mode mirrorplayback --trace=gs://prod-traces/2026-03-16/02/*.ndjson 
  --sample-filter "cohort=small_users" --seed 42 --anon-level low 
  --kernel-hints off --kv-prewarm true 
  --out /tmp/mirror-rerun42 
```
Olivia H.: doing it now. expect ~20m. will post perfbot summary when done
(20m later)
PerfBot: run=1719206000, cohort=small_users-rerun42, throughput=435 tok/s, p50=26ms, p95=121ms, kernel_mix=[fused_gemm:77%, aten_gemm:23%], kv_hit_rate=0.79, checksum_mismatch=0.001
Sam K.: that's telling. with fixed seed + low anon we recovered expected kernel distribution and kv hit. So sanitizer/anon pipeline was changing token lengths and hurting cache warming -> different kernel path choices
Lee R.: agree. two remediation options: (A) improve anonymizer to preserve token-length distribution (we already have an opt-in preserve_lens flag), (B) make kernel selector more robust to small len shifts by softening thresholds (fallback smoothing)
Anya P.: ops note: any change that preserves lengths in anon pipeline has privacy implications. Need privacy review before flipping preserve_lens=true for mirror runs. We can add an internal-only flag for fidelity testing but mark it non-prod and restricted
Olivia H.: next steps: 1) re-run ensemble of 3 cohorts with seed=42+low-anon to get apples-to-apples baseline, 2) add a harness flag `--anon-fidelity` that toggles length preservation (internal only), 3) propose selector smoothing patch (will draft PR)
Sam K.: also we should capture per-request kernel decision logs in harness (tiny id + chosen_kernel) so we can correlate token_len -> kernel. Add kv_warmup_trace with timestamps to compare warmup curves
Lee R.: I'll take the PR for selector smoothing. Olivia can you open an RFC in eng-runtime with the perf numbers and proposed options? Include the perfbot run ids and the exact config diff
Olivia H.: will do. RFC link when up. tagging @security for privacy gating when RFC ready :security: 
Anya P.: noted. please include a short privacy test matrix (risk, mitigations, auditor)
Sam K.: nice catch Olivia. summary: harness diffs were driven by anonymization-induced length shifts causing different kernel choices and slower kv warming. Fixes: deterministic seeding for apples-to-apples, anon-fidelity toggle for internal tests, and selector smoothing to reduce sensitivity
Olivia H.: thanks all, will track in the RFC and follow up in this thread when PRs land :thumbsup:
